body:
**Triage: `documentation` · `priority:p2` · `pm:queue` · `domain:spec` · type `Task`.** First grading, `finding` comes off. ⭐ **Promoted to the family anchor** — see the scope note below.

**`domain:spec`**: the map is `packages/spec/scripts/build-skill-references.ts:98-109` and the `_index.md` files are generated from it. ⛔ The generated indexes are **not** hand-edited.

**p2 because the index ships to third parties** via `npx skills add`, and both directions mislead an agent reader: five schemas are advertised that the body never teaches (three with **zero consumers** outside `packages/spec`), so an agent following the index `Read`s into `node_modules` for guidance that does not exist; and `ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts` — the schema behind a built-in skill the body *does* name — is absent, so the one pointer worth having is missing.

## Ruling: narrow the map, add `solution-blueprint`. ⛔ Do not widen the body.

- **Narrow** is restoration, not a capability removal, and that distinction is why it is dispatchable: an index entry is a *pointer*, and pointing at a schema the body cannot help with is the defect. The schema keeps existing and stays importable; only the false promise goes. (Stated explicitly so a reviewer can object to the reasoning rather than to the outcome.)
- **Add `solution-blueprint`** — the card is right that this half is unambiguous in either direction, because the body already names the built-in skill it backs.
- ⛔ **Widening the body is off the table for this card.** It fights the value gate on measured grounds (zero consumers for three of the five) and the SKILL.md ratchet ceiling is 6,806 tokens. If someone believes a specific surface deserves teaching, that is a skills-flight card with its own budget, ⛔ not a rider here.

## ⭐ Scope: run the census for all eleven packages, not just this one

The card's own closing line is the important one — *"Worth checking whether the same unreconciled shape exists for the other 10 packages' `SKILL_MAP` entries; this audit only measured `objectstack-ai`."* **It does**: #14466 found the same shape on `objectstack-automation` (the index routes to the ADR-0020-**retired** `state-machine.zod.ts` and omits both per-node `config` schemas), filed independently within the hour.

⇒ Two independent discoveries in one hour is a class, not two incidents. ⛔ Reconciling one package per card produces eleven cards and eleven rulings for one mechanical mismatch. **This card carries the census** — for each of the eleven `SKILL_MAP` entries, the set difference in both directions against what its SKILL.md teaches — and applies the ruling above uniformly. #14466 stays open as the member card holding `automation`'s specific facts; ⛔ do not close it as a duplicate, its retired-schema pointer is a distinct defect worth its own line in the changeset.

⚠️ **`state-machine.zod.ts` being ADR-0020-retired is the sharpest instance and should gate the design**: whatever reconciliation lands must make a retired schema in the map *impossible*, not merely *corrected once* — otherwise the census is a one-off and the next retirement re-opens it. If deriving the map from a checkable source is out of reach, say so in the PR rather than hand-fixing eleven lists.

**Dedup accepted as run** — one targeted `search_issues` validated in-session by a control query that returned its known hit. ⚠️ Worth repeating for future filers: that control is what makes the result readable, because `search_issues` returns intermittent false zeros in this repo (#13326).

Size/model suggestion: M, `sonnet` — the census is the work; the edits are small once it exists.

"whatever reconciliation lands must make a retired schema in the map *impossible*, not merely *corrected once* … If deriving the map from a checkable source is out of reach, say so in the PR rather than hand-fixing eleven lists." Triage 5506975178 (#14466): drop `automation/state-machine.zod.ts`; the omitted per-node `config` schemas (`automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts`, `automation/io-node-config.zod.ts`) join — "its retired-schema pointer is a distinct defect worth its own line in the changeset". Triage 5515135764 (#14562): "The class has **two** mechanisms … ⛔ Do not build the `SKILL_MAP`-only gate and declare the class closed." Seat ruling for #14562 (claim 5536681114): drop `data/date-macros.zod.ts` from the formula entry; no duplicate-ownership rule; a loud one-owner guard instead. Triage 5514974653 (#14565): decide the closure rule's feasibility FIRST and say so in the PR body — reachability rule if it can be made precise, else a per-package transitive allowlist/denylist beside `SKILL_MAP`; ⛔ no hand edit of `_index.md`. ⛔ No SKILL.md body widened; ⛔ no `.zod.ts` edited.

**PM mechanism assumptions (verify; falsify freely).** (a) `SKILL_MAP` on `origin/main` `9c1bcda3` has **9** entries (data · query · ai · api · automation · ui · platform · i18n · formula; the triage said eleven — count and report), 9 generated `skills/*/references/_index.md` files. (b) A checkable source for "retired": the file header of `automation/state-machine.zod.ts` carries the ADR-0020 retirement in prose only; the ADR-0087 registry (`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/retired-defs/**`, `RETIRED_DEFS_BY_MAJOR`) names retired *defs*, not files; the liveness ledger classifies properties. The dev decides whether any of these is a precise source for a "no retired schema in the map" guard; if none is, the PR says so (the triage accepts that answer) and the guard the PR still ships is the mechanical one: every `SKILL_MAP` path must exist and be exported by an entry, and appears in at most one package (loud refusal at generation). (c) The census output (per package: advertised-not-taught, taught-not-advertised) belongs in the PR body as a table; the SKILL.md bodies are read, never edited. (d) `check:skill-refs` is the drift gate (`tsx scripts/build-skill-references.ts --check`); `gen:skill-refs` regenerates; a generator with a test file gets a negative test for each guard. (e) Changeset vs `skip-changeset`: follow PR #14737's precedent on this generator; read that PR's files before choosing.

**PM suggested route (optional).** One commit per member: anchor (census + the `objectstack-ai` narrowing + `ai/solution-blueprint.zod.ts` + the guards), #14466, #14562, #14565 (closure rule or list), then one regeneration commit if the generator emits everything at once. PR body: the census table, the feasibility answer for the closure step, the guard(s) and their negative tests, the net line delta in `skills/**`.

**Surface, budget, gates, report.** File surface = the anchor claim 5536679159 (stop on breach). **Net line budget in `skills/**`: ≤ +6 lines across all nine `_index.md` files combined**; every added line one of the members' named additions; over budget ⇒ stop and report, ⛔ never raise it. Derive gates from your actual paths after the last commit (`node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands`, no path args); at minimum `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:skill-refs`, `check:skill-examples` (build its prerequisite first), `check:llms-txt`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:scripts-typecheck` (or the `typecheck` composite), `pnpm check:doc-authoring`, `pnpm check:nul-bytes`, `node scripts/check-system-context-census.mjs`, the skills token ratchet family the derivation names. Report: `os-dev-report` first as a comment on this anchor (members get a one-line pointer each), then as the return; machine-checkable fields only, plus the per-member criterion verdicts and the `skills/**` net line delta.
